annotations.title: Check an inbox's DNS and discovery

description: Checks whether AI agents are led from the business's website and DNS to its agent inbox, and whether the inbox answers at inbox.<domain> (or the host given): for a business's own AI. Reads the inbox's DNS record (against target, when given) and manifest, the site's robots.txt (no AI assistant kept out), and five ways the domain can point to the inbox: four on the website (/.well-known/agent-inbox.json, a line in llms.txt, <link rel="agent-inbox">, a schema.org potentialAction) and a _agent-inbox TXT record. ready needs one of the four on the website. Every item not in place comes with the exact record, line or file to add (fix_lines: the text to paste). Reads the site as a browser would, and nothing it asked crawlers not to read; what it read is kept for a minute.

domain.description: The business's own domain, like salon.example (a URL is read as its domain).

host.description: Where the inbox answers, when not inbox.<domain>: the domain itself or a name under it.

target.description: The CNAME target the host must point to, when known (a hosted inbox's Connect page shows it).

name: check_dns

domain.description: The business's own domain (its registrable domain).

host.description: Where the inbox answers: inbox.<domain> unless another was named.

fix.description: The exact record, line or file to add, when it is not ok.

fix_lines.description: The text to paste, alone, when the fix is one.

need.description: required: the inbox cannot be reached without it; recommended and optional: ways the domain leads to it.

state.description: ok: found as it should be; missing; wrong: there, pointing elsewhere; blocked: robots.txt keeps AI assistants out; unreadable: could not be read, with why.

next.description: The one step worth doing first.

platform.description: The site's platform, when its homepage (or the network's last read of it) shows one of these.

ready.description: The inbox answers at its host, robots.txt keeps no AI assistant out, and at least one way on the business's website leads to it (the DNS pointer alone does not).

site_ways.description: How many of those are on the website (all but dns_txt).

state.description: What the check found, as a whole; ready is state ready.

ways.description: How many of well_known, llms_txt, link, schema_org and dns_txt lead to it.

title: Check an inbox's DNS and discovery
